judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed calendar date subject to Contract Time adjustments; the wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the printed 4.3's duration-from-commencement formula while revised 4.1 makes commencement contingent on permits, so the relationship between a conditional start and a fixed finish is unresolved; the 4.4 bonus also keys off 'the established date.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A sum to be determined' fixes no amount and no method, 'the work is determined to be substantially complete' names no decider, and the bonus is then 'divided between the key management staff, as determined by the Owner'—an obligation that may be too indefinite to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Contract Sum in 5.1.1 is Cost of the Work plus Fee with no bonus component, A201 9.8.4 makes the Architect the determiner of Substantial Completion, and no counterpart liquidated-damages term exists; the bonus sits awkwardly in the payment scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Dense with soft terms—'fast-track basis,' 'current best estimate,' 'industry-standard figures,' pricing 'as agreed with Owner,' and a termination right in the Owner's 'sole and absolute discretion' if the Preliminary Budget cannot be 'negotiated to the satisfaction of Owner.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates a budget-and-Change-Order regime that displaces 5.2.1's blank Guaranteed Maximum Price and 12.1.5's GMP-based schedule of values, overlaps Article 10's bidding procedure, and adds a termination right outside Article 13 and A201 Article 14. Reconciling those is a genuine whole-instrument problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Capable of being prevented through timely notice of an unsafe condition' is a counterfactual standard that will be argued about after any emergency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The printed 7.7.2 remains in the Agreement without these carve-outs, and A201 10.6.1 lets the Contractor act 'at the Contractor's discretion' with compensation determined under 4.3 and Article 7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds an insurance-maintenance proviso to an already conditional reimbursement; the conditions are stated but cumulative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The unrevised 7.7.3 is still printed in the Agreement and 8.1.6 cross-refers to '7.7.3 of this Agreement,' so which text that cross-reference picks up is a question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list of Fee-covered items ending in broad categories ('all main office expenses,' 'estimating/project purchasing costs and expenses') whose overlap with site costs is not marked off.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is numbered 8.1.8 but replaces a paragraph about the Guaranteed Maximum Price with an entirely different subject, and it cuts across 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.6.6 and 8.1.1-8.1.4, so what remains of the printed 8.1.8 is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A seven-day notice condition with a stated purpose; the obligation is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplements 9.1's allocation of discounts and 9.2's credit mechanism without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All in form and substance satisfactory to Owner and Architect' is a subjective gate on payment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carries the same number as the printed 12.1.4 substantiation requirement, so two differently worded 12.1.4s govern the same Application for Payment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed, itemised reporting requirement; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 9.3.1 and 9.6.2-9.6.3 on subcontractor payment information.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The $2,500 threshold and the classes of waiver required are specific; whether waivers must be conditional or unconditional is left open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 9.3.3 (title warranty) and 9.10.2 (releases at final payment) address the same subject at different stages without contradiction; the Addendum 12.2.2 lien-free endorsement is a further layer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure catch-all ('such other information, documentation, and material as Owner or the Architect reasonably may require') sitting after two specific items, so its reach against the enumerated list is exactly the ejusdem generis question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the printed 12.1.4's 'any other evidence required by the Owner or Architect,' so the layered demands are cumulative rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Five percent retainage is stated, but the fixed-sum fee formula still depends on 'a reasonable estimate of the probable Cost of the Work upon its completion,' a figure never fixed in the contract.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts the printed 12.1.7.3, whose retainage is 'N/A percent,' and sits against 12.1.8's ten percent subcontractor retainage and A201 9.8.5 on release of retainage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single added condition; 'duly published and recorded' has a definite statutory meaning in Hawaii.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds a third condition to 12.2.1 and interlocks with the revised 12.2.2's fifty-day period, but neither text says who must publish and record the Notice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Whichever is earlier' between fifty days after recordation and five business days after a lien-free endorsement can make payment fall due on a date that has nothing to do with the Architect's certificate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts the printed 12.2.2 (30 days after the final Certificate) and can require payment before the conditions in 12.2.1 and the accountants' review in 12.2.3 are complete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Naming 'Mr. or Mrs. Paul Stephens or Mary Williamson' as 'the Owner's representative' leaves it unclear whether any one of them may bind the Owner alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 2.1.1.1 names Mary Williamson as the authorized representative but permits action by Paul H. Stephens, Elle M. Stephens or Mary Williamson, while A201 2.1.1 contemplates a single designee with express authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A survival and materiality preamble; standard and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fills the blank 'Other provisions' slot of Article 14, which 7.2.2 and 8.1.1 cross-refer to for cost purposes; the warranties themselves have nothing to do with those cost carve-outs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A present-tense solvency warranty extended to 'the Subcontractors,' who at execution are not yet identified—an odd but readable representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 5.2.1 contemplates subcontractors being proposed after award, so warranting their solvency at signing is hard to square with the procurement sequence in 10.1 and Addendum 6.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A capability warranty in ordinary terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Addendum Article 2 [Revised] and A201 3.4; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A licensing and authorisation warranty stated in absolute terms; 'quasi-public authorities' is the only loose phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with A201 3.7.2 compliance with law and 13.1.1 Hawaii governing law; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A site-familiarity representation in conventional terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates A201 1.5.2 and overlaps 3.2.1, and it sits against A201 4.3.4's claim right for concealed or unknown conditions, though the two are usually read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line identification of the Agreement as modified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the provision that reconciles the Addendum with Article 1's statement that the Agreement governs inconsistencies, so it reduces rather than creates conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line identification of the General Conditions as modified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It corrects the printed 15.1.2's '1991 edition' slip and matches the Supplementary Conditions' own incorporation language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Incorporates A201 'Articles 1 through 14 inclusive' by reference—precise, though it silently omits nothing since A201 ends at Article 14.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches 15.1.2 as revised; the Agreement's Article 1 priority rule still sits above it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence—'the unaltered provision of the General Conditions shall remain in effect'—can be read either as preserving unmodified portions or as preserving the very provision that has been modified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That reading matters directly for revisions such as 2.4.1, where the Supplementary Condition drops A201's second three-day notice; if the 'unaltered provision' survives, the revision is neutered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Wherever ... a matter requires notice to, communication with, or the consent, approval or concurrence of the Architect' is a sweeping substitution, coupled with a disclaimer that the Owner has no responsibility for means and methods 'notwithstanding any of the rights and authority granted the Owner.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 gives the Architect independent certifying and deciding functions (4.2.5, 4.2.7, 4.2.12, 4.4), and 4.1.2 forbids modifying the Architect's duties without the Architect's written consent; adding an Owner veto to every such act cuts across that scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The better quality or greater quantity of Work' and 'the more stringent requirement,' applied 'either or both,' is a classic source of dispute about what the Contractor must supply at no extra cost.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement's Article 1 resolves inconsistencies in favour of the Agreement, A201 1.2.1 makes the documents complementary and limits performance to what is 'reasonably inferable,' and 5.2.6 addresses further development; the three rules point different ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise precedence rule for dimensions and drawing scales.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 15.1.5 enumerates no Drawings and dates them 'TBD,' so the rule operates on documents the Agreement never identifies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No extra charge or compensation will be allowed on account of differences between actual dimensions and the dimensions indicated on the Drawings' is a flat bar whose interaction with the verification duty in the same paragraph is not spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: In a cost-of-the-work contract all properly incurred costs are reimbursable under Article 7, and A201 3.2.3 and 4.3.4 preserve claims for conditions differing from the documents; a no-extra-charge rule is hard to reconcile with both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Minor change ... due to actual field conditions' with a submittal-and-approval requirement; the threshold word 'minor' is soft but familiar.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 7.4.1 lets the Architect order minor changes without Owner approval and without a change in Contract Sum, while Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 requires a Change Order for any change in Contract Sum or Time.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It names one person as 'the Owner's authorized representative' and then permits any of three named individuals to take any action, decision or direction—two inconsistent designations in one paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 14.3 and Addendum 14.3 [Revised] give still different lists, and A201 2.1.1 requires designation of a representative 'who shall have express authority to bind the Owner'; who could bind the Owner is genuinely unsettled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single seven-day cure period with a Change Order deduction mechanism; internally clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 2.4.1 requires a second written notice and a further three-day period before the Owner may self-help, and Supplementary Condition preamble says unaltered General Conditions provisions remain in effect—so two incompatible cure procedures are in play.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall be deemed attached to Document A111 as a part of the Contract Documents' converts a Contractor-prepared schedule into contract text automatically, and 'all activities and events' is expansive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 1.1.1 and 1.1.2 allow amendment only by Modification and Article 1/15 enumerate the Contract Documents, while A201 3.10.1-3.10.3 treat the schedule as informational with performance 'in general accordance'; the deeming provision does not fit either.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Phase names ('75% Design Development Phase') and the requirement that cost estimates 'become part of the Contract Documents' leave the legal effect of each estimate unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same deeming problem as 3.10.4 against A201 1.1.2's Modification-only rule, plus overlap with Addendum 6.5's Preliminary Budget procedure and the fixed completion date in revised 4.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A submittal and competence warranty; 'expertise and experience in the trade' is qualitative but ordinary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 3.12.10 says the Contractor is not required to provide professional design services unless the Contract Documents require them, which this clause partly does by requiring a licensed engineer when the Architect, Owner or law requires.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed pleading requirement for time claims; each element is specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplements A201 4.3.7.1's notice requirement without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is convoluted ('a separate increase ... for each one of the number of causes of delay which may have concurrent or interrelated effects'), and concurrent-delay allocation is inherently contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 8.3.1 entitles the Contractor to extension for delays beyond its control, so how a concurrent delay partly outside the Contractor's fault is treated is left unresolved between the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It bars increases based on 'course of conduct or dealings,' 'express or implied acceptance of alterations or additions,' and unjust enrichment 'whether or not there is, in fact, any unjust enrichment,' subject only to two cross-referenced exceptions—broad, one-sided drafting whose exceptions define its reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: In a cost-plus contract the Contract Sum floats with the Cost of the Work under 5.1.1 and Article 7, and A201 4.3.4, 4.4.5, 7.3 and 7.4 plus Addendum 6.5 all provide non-Change-Order routes to adjustment; a Change-Order-only rule is hard to harmonise with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Final settlement of all matters relating to the change ... including all direct and indirect costs' is a broad preclusion resting on the scope of 'relating to.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 7.3.9 and 4.3.2 contemplate later claims and adjustments, and Addendum 6.5 issues Change Orders progressively as items are priced, so the finality of each Change Order interacts with an evolving budget.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The joint-payment election and the three-part disclaimer are drafted precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary' opening runs against A201 9.6.2, 9.6.4 and 9.6.7 on payments to and holding funds for subcontractors, but the disclaimer resolves the obvious tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear delivery requirement and a clear condition on the final Certificate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds a condition to final certification beyond those in 12.2.1 and 12.2.3 and beyond A201 9.10.1-9.10.2, and 'accepted by the Owner' gives the Owner an extra gate over the Architect's certificate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes tools and equipment whose capital value 'is not included in the Work'—a definite carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with A201 11.4.1's 'all-risk' cover of the Work and with the reimbursement of tools and rentals under 7.5.1-7.5.2 and Exhibit C; no direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reciprocal cost-shifting rule with a stated causation test ('properly attributable thereto').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It largely duplicates A201 11.4.1.2's last sentence for the Owner's side and adds attorneys' fees, which sits against 7.6.8's exclusion of legal costs arising from Owner-Contractor disputes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exhibit says hand-tool cost 'shall be borne by the Contractor' and in the next sentence adds a flat 5% of payroll 'to cover the cost of these hand tools,' and the tool list is doubly open-ended ('include, but are not limited to ... etc.').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.5.1 and 7.5.2 make hand tools not customarily owned by workers reimbursable at cost or rental, 8.1.5 excludes rentals except as provided in 7.5.2, and 8.1.7 excludes anything not expressly described in Article 7; a percentage add-on fits none of them, and Article 1 says the Agreement governs inconsistencies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It calls a 1% -of-labour-and-subcontractor-cost charge 'the insurance premium for the General Liability Policy,' which is a billing formula rather than a premium and may not match what is actually paid.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.6.1 reimburses only 'that portion of insurance and bond premiums that can be directly attributed to this Contract,' and 8.1.7 excludes anything not expressly described in Article 7; the formula and the attribution test can produce different numbers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All direct costs except Subcontract costs' is then expanded by a self-defined and open list of vendor costs 'including; rubbish hauling ... freight charges. etc.,' leaving the exempt category's boundary uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.6.2 reimburses taxes 'imposed by a governmental authority that are related to the Work,' whereas this exhibit computes a percentage on job costs; with 8.1.7's exclusion of unenumerated costs the two treatments must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional list closing with the exclusion of bidding documents 'unless specifically enumerated in the Agreement'; conventional and precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5 deem schedules and cost estimates part of the Contract Documents without any Modification, and Addendum 6.5 adds the Preliminary Budget as an exhibit, which this definition does not contemplate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Integration language plus the rule that the Contract 'may be amended or modified only by Modification'; the disclaimers of third-party relationships are stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly meets Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4/3.10.5, which make later-prepared schedules and estimates part of the Contract Documents automatically, and it duplicates the Agreement's own integration clause in Article 1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard definition of the Work covering labour, materials, equipment and services.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement Article 2 and its Addendum revision; nothing conflicting located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition of the Project; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 6.1.1 on separate contractors and with the Agreement's project identification.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of the Drawings by content; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 15.1.5 lists no Drawings and dates them 'TBD,' so the defined term has no identified referent in the enumerated Contract Documents.
